summary: BGP routers report problems with a NOTIFICATION message, and one error category covers the finite state machine (FSM). This RFC defines subcodes for it so operators get more detail about what went wrong and can correlate network events. It updates RFC 4271.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 6608 gives BGP Finite State Machine errors subcodes that identify where an unexpected message arrived. A BGP speaker sends the subcode in a NOTIFICATION to help operators diagnose the session problem.

subtitle: BGP subcodes that explain which state received an unexpected message.

tldr.problem: The generic BGP Finite State Machine error does not identify which session state received an unexpected message.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines subcodes for unexpected messages in OpenSent, OpenConfirm, and Established states, plus an unspecified-error value.
tldr.outcome: BGP implementations must include the appropriate subcode in a NOTIFICATION for these FSM errors; the RFC updates RFC 4271.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 6608's status as Proposed Standard. The RFC updates RFC 4271 with more specific BGP FSM error subcodes.

sections.title: More Detail for BGP FSM Errors
sections.content:
The RFC defines subcodes for BGP Finite State Machine errors to help network operators diagnose problems and correlate network events. The additional information can also help developers in lab situations.

It updates RFC 4271 by requiring BGP implementations to include appropriate FSM Error subcodes in NOTIFICATION messages for these errors.
sections.plainLanguage: A more specific error tells an operator which BGP state received an unexpected message. That detail can make troubleshooting clearer.

sections.title: The Defined Error Subcodes
sections.content:
The defined values are 0 for Unspecified Error, 1 for an unexpected message in OpenSent, 2 for an unexpected message in OpenConfirm, and 3 for an unexpected message in Established.

When a speaker receives an unexpected message in one of those states, it sends a NOTIFICATION with the Finite State Machine Error code and the matching subcode. The one-octet Data field identifies the type of unexpected message.
sections.plainLanguage: The subcode identifies which of three BGP states received an unexpected message. The notification also includes a one-byte value identifying the message type.

sections.title: Operational Security Consideration
sections.content:
The RFC notes that these more detailed errors could make it easier to identify or fingerprint a BGP implementation. Operators should consider that possibility when deciding how to deploy BGP.

The subcodes provide diagnostic information; this RFC does not change the underlying BGP session state machine.
sections.plainLanguage: Detailed error responses can reveal information about an implementation. Operators should account for that when deciding how BGP errors are exposed.
